details.readme:
The open-source AI video editor: create, edit, remake.

Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Download the app · Quickstart · Showcase · Catalog · Docs · Discord · X · YouTube

HyperFrames is HeyGen's AI video editor for people and agents. Describe a video, bring your own footage, or remake a video you love, and get a real project you can change down to the frame: ask for a bigger title, a faster cut or new captions, and it changes just that. Underneath, HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework (Apache 2.0) for turning HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. No React required. ## Three ways to use it | | Best for | Start | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **HyperFrames Studio app** | Anyone, no code. Describe a video or drop in your footage, then edit by typing or pointing. Use the built-in agent on Pro, or your own Claude Code or Codex. | [Download for Mac, Windows or Linux](https://hyperframes.studio/studio/download?src=github-readme) (free plan) | | **Your coding agent** | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents. | `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes` | | **Claude, ChatGPT or Grok** (beta) | Making a video in a chat, nothing to install. ChatGPT: Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces. | Connect [HyperFrames by HeyGen](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/mcp?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme), listed in [Claude's connector directory](https://claude.com/connectors/hyperframes-heygen) | The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.studio/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) has a free plan. [Pro](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) ($25 a month) adds top video, image, voice and music models (HeyGen Video 1, Seedance 2.5, Lyria 3 Pro and more) and 25,000 credits a month. ## Made with HyperFrames

Script-based editing

Captions on your video
Remake any video

Launch video from your website
Faceless explainer

Real-UI motion graphics

3D one-take trailer

Remotion project, ported

Click any clip to watch it with sound. ## What you can make | Video | How | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Branded UGC videos for TikTok and Instagram from your own phone clips: captions, music, text hooks, fast client revisions | The Studio app: drop in your footage, then edit by typing or pointing | | Video podcast episodes: line up a multi-camera recording, cut to whoever is talking, clean up the sound, add captions | The Studio app's podcast edit | | Product demos, tutorials, launch videos and feature announcements, from your website or a screen recording | Paste your URL into the Studio app, or ask your agent | | Explainer and faceless YouTube episodes from your topic, script or voiceover | Ask for one; [`/style-sampling`](skills/style-sampling) for five proven series styles | | Remake a video you love, then make it yours | [`/reverse-any-video`](skills/reverse-any-video)

details.readme:
The open-source Claude Motion & CapCut alternative

Install · Agents · Use cases & remakes · Why OpenMotion · Setup & architecture · Community

**English** · [简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/README.ja.md)
# OpenMotion OpenMotion is a **full-stack agentic video** studio and an **open-source alternative to Claude Motion and CapCut**. Upload a reference video or paste a social video link to **recreate it with your own brand kit and copy**. - 🎬 **Full-stack video recreation.** Code video with HTML. Your agent breaks down the reference, rebuilds its shots and transitions, and generates missing assets. Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project. - 🔑 **BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys.** OpenMotion is free and open source. Recreate videos in [your local agent](#agent-wall) with your own API keys. Supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, and WorkBuddy. - 🧩 OpenMotion introduces **Motion.md**, a Markdown format for shot order, timing and transitions. Use it to share how a brand film works, shot by shot. - 🎛️ **Images, video, music and voice.** Create artwork with GPT Image 2.6, add a shot with Seedance 2.5, score it with Suno and narrate it with Eleven v4. [Explore the models and providers](#model-wall). ### Install from ChatGPT Marketplace **One-click installation. No manual configuration required.** Once installed, create motion videos from scratch, recreate reference videos, or start from a template—all in your conversation. **[Install OpenMotion in ChatGPT →](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6a742d13e88481919b42002864b1bb26)** ### Install in your agent Install the main Skill with the [Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): ```sh npx skills add nexu-io/openmotion --skill openmotion ``` Then ask your agent: **Use OpenMotion to connect Cloud MCP, then help me make a video.** The Skill connects directly to the hosted Streamable HTTP `/mcp` endpoint via OAuth 2.1 without installing a local runtime, and reuses an existing working connection. Installing the Skill alone copies instructions; it does not yet connect MCP. Copy this instruction into your agent to connect OpenMotion Cloud MCP: ```text Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/docs/install.md and follow the instructions to connect OpenMotion in the current agent. ``` After OAuth authorization, the agent opens the cloud template library and shows the localized welcome followed by three curated project-preview cards via a native MCP App, self-contained HTML document, DSH card, or text fallback. Each onboarding samples three distinct entries from the curated pool of four without waiting for native MCP tool reload or fetching remote reference films for inline previews. Preview a card, choose **Recreate template**, then send your brief to start creating. [Cloud MCP connection guide](docs/install.md) · [Onboarding reply rules](docs/install.md#installation-success-reply) ### Legacy local source & npm installation (optional) Cloud MCP setup above is the default Agent connection path. For self-hosted deployments see [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md). Legacy local source/stdio setup and published npm application recipes remain archived for explicit local use: ```text Read https://releases.open-design.ai/motion and follow the instructions to install and connect the published npm application in the current agent. ``` [Archived legacy local source & npm guide](docs/templates/legacy-npm-install.md) · [npm installation and diagnostics](docs/npm-installation.md). Published npm versions can lag behind this checkout. ### Run the repository locally Use Git, npm and Node.js 26.11.1: ```sh git -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.required=false clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion.git cd openmotion npm ci npm run build:studio npm start ``` Open the actual `studioUrl` or `previewUrl` printed at startup, then choose **Template library**. Studio and MCP read the templates in this checkout. To connect your agent to this same copy, follow [source setup and MCP configuration](#agent-setup). [Clone size and optional media](docs/repository-storage.md) ### Start from an existing project Import a **HyperFrames project ZIP** into OpenMotion to continue editing its composition and local assets. Compress the project folder, open **All projects → Import projects**, then select the imported copy to edit in Studio or with your Agent. Import creates an independent copy and requires a supported native project structure. [Step-by-step import guide, required files and compatibility](docs/project-archives.md#import-from-hyperframes) **22 local agents** · [Choose your agent](#choose-agent)

## 🎞️ Use cases and remake examples Explore product demos, brand films, talking-head videos and more. The previews below show reference videos. **[Browse the full template library →](https://open-design.ai/templates/)** — Find more templates, full videos, Motion.md and recreation instructions. ### AI recuts & revisions

OpenAI · Build a story from multiple scenes
Connect different scenes around one narrative idea, then expand into a broader montage.
View template
Anthropic · Recut a making-of collage
Layer clips and screenshots in sequence, keeping the main title readable above them.
View template
### Product launches & demos

Notion · Show a problem, then the solution
Move from crowded tasks to coordinated agents; adapt the sequence to your own product.
View template
OpenAI · Turn demand into a product reveal
Build momentum with overlapping requests, then reveal the app in one clear beat.
View template
### Brand films & motion

Kimi · Connect worlds through motion
Use code strips, offset slices and transitions to connect a series of brand scenes.
View template

repository.description: The AI-native engine for teams and their agents. Multi-harness, multi-agent, self-hosted.

details.readme:
**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) > **中文文档入口：[文档目录](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [安装与启动](docs/getting-started.md) · [开发指南](docs/development.md)**
# SoduWork ## The AI-native engine for teams and their agents **A chat ends with an answer. A SoduWork request ends when the person who asked signs off.** **Multi-harness · Multi-agent · Self-hosted** Works with Pi · OpenCode · DeepSeek Harness · Qwen Code · Kimi Code · Codex Harness · Codex **Run from source** ```sh git clone https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork cd SoduWork ``` | Platform | Start command | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `sh start.sh --desktop` | | Windows PowerShell | `.\start.cmd --desktop` | | Windows Command Prompt | `start.cmd --desktop` | For source setup, we recommend [Python 3.12.x](https://www.python.org/downloads/) and [Node.js 22.x](https://nodejs.org/) (22.19.0 or later in that series). The clone command uses [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads). **[Windows desktop app](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest)** | [Website](https://soduwork.ai) | [Live demo](https://soduwork.ai) | [Documentation](docs/README.md) | [Docs website](https://dev.soduwork.ai) | [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mdiri-ai/SoduWork)](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#quick-start) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2.svg)](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)
--- ## What SoduWork can do for you | | | | --- | --- | | **One harness does the work, another reviews it** | Pick Pi to do the work. OpenCode, on a different model, reviews it against the acceptance criteria. If the review fails, the work goes back with the reasons. | | **Hand a request to a colleague's agent** | People and AI work together: you file a request, AI writes the acceptance criteria, and you assign it to yourself or a colleague. The assignee's agent does the work and reviews it, and a person signs off. Everyone on the request can see who did what. | | **Turn one person's know-how into a team asset** | When you and AI get a task right, save the chat as a plugin. After review, anyone on the team can use it and contribute improvements, with access granted as needed. | ## Core ideas
**🔀 Smart dispatch** **The right agent and model for each job.** - Pick a harness for each step and switch mid-conversation - Routine steps on cheap or local models, strong models where it matters - Long tasks go to your own cloud runner **🛡️ Built-in governance** **Your organization decides which AI does what, and where.** - Plugins are reviewed before they are shared, granted to teams or people, and can be revoked - Roles, usage, cost and an audit log - Self-hosted **✅ Verified delivery** **Set the bar first. Done means the requester signed off.** - Every request carries its acceptance criteria - A separate AI review checks each one - A person makes the final call
## Quick start > SoduWork is in public beta. Try it and tell us what you think, and evaluate it before using it in production. Clone the repository with Git or extract a source archive. See the [source setup guide](docs/getting-started.en.md) for prerequisites. From the repository root, run `sh start.sh --desktop` on macOS/Linux, `.\start.cmd --desktop` in Windows PowerShell, or `start.cmd --desktop` in Command Prompt. If Windows says a command “is not recognized”, check which command it names. For `git`, `python` or `node`, check that the corresponding tool is installed and on `PATH`, then reopen Command Prompt. See the [source setup guide](docs/getting-started.en.md). The first run installs dependencies, then starts the Hub, the admin console and the desktop client on this computer. Set a password for the `admin` account (12–128 characters) when asked. Then add a model provider under **Model catalog** in the admin console, start a chat in the client and try a small task. Pi is built in. ### Already added an API key? Start here 1. **Add a chat model as well.** Under **Capabilities → Model catalog**, find the service you connected, choose **Add model**, enter the provider's exact model ID, select **Chat model**, and save. Saving a service credential alone does not create a selectable model. 2. **Open the desktop client and sign in to the same Hub.** Use `--desktop` when starting from source. The browser admin console configures the service; check that **Connection** on the desktop sign-in screen points to that same Hub. 3. **Choose New conversation, Pi, and the model you added.** Pi uses the SoduWork model catalog. Codex uses its own account and needs its own sign-in; it does not automatically use this API key. 4. **Try a small task.** For example: “Turn these fictional meeting notes into an action table with owner and due date. Mark missing information as unconfirmed: Alex will organize the requirements by Friday; Sam will check the quotation.” Check the returned table against the notes. 5. **Create a requirement when you need assignment and acceptance.** Describe the goal, inputs and acceptance criteria, open **Arrange execution**, choose an Agent and model, and inspect the delivery before accepting it. A normal conversation does not require a project, plugin or automation first. For the first message, use an **OpenAI-compatible chat model with Pi**. A successful connection probe does not guarantee a successful inference: balance, model permissions and protocol support still matter. If the Agent list is empty, check **Agent management** and the Runner connection. If the model list is empty, check that the model exists, is enabled, and both interfaces use the same Hub. See [Run from source: send your first AI message](docs/getting-started.en.md#send-your-first-ai-message) for field-by-field setup and troubleshooting.
Try the live demo Download the client from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest), enter `https://service.soduwork.ai` under **Connection** on the sign-in screen, then sign up and sign in. > The demo is for evaluation only. Don't upload real business data or anything sensitive.
Install the desktop client Follow the illustrated [desktop installation and first conversation guide](docs/desktop-quickstart.en.md). | OS | Package | | --- | --- | | Windows | `SoduWork--Setup.exe` | | macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `SoduWork--mac-.dmg` | | Linux | `SoduWork--linux.deb` / `.rpm` / `.tar.gz` | Download from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases). On first launch, enter your Hub address under **Connection**, then sign in. On macOS, if you see "cannot verify the developer", open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**.
Deploy for a team with Docker With Docker installed and running, from the repository root: ```bash python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py up python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py credentials # show the initial admin password ``` This starts the Hub, the admin console and PostgreSQL on one server. Put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it to open it to your team. See [Deploy with Docker](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/docker) and [Deploy for a team](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/deploy).
Ports, data folders and troubleshooting are in [Run from source](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/run-from-source) and the [FAQ](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/faq). ## Why SoduWork AI agents give everyone fast output. What no one gets for free is trust in that output — or a way to keep what worked. That's where individuals and teams get stuck alike: | The problem | What SoduWork does | | --- | --- | | **Fast output, slow trust** — whether you work alone or in a team, the time AI saves goes back into checking what it produced | **The request is the spec.** Criteria set before work starts; a separate AI review checks each one; a person signs off | | **What worked dies in a chat thread** — for one person, it's last month's perfect run you can't reproduce; for a team, it's one person's method nobody else can use | **Get it right once, keep it as a plugin.** Reuse it yourself or publish it for everyone — every improvement reaches everyone | | **A drawer full of AI tools** — three subscriptions and no standard for which one does what | **One workbench, your playbook.** Your plugins run on every harness. Switch mid-conversation, keep your history and files | | **Results that never enter the workflow** — output gets copy-pasted around, and every handoff re-explains the background | **Issues that carry the context.** People and agents pick up where it left off, with a full record of who did what | ## How it works Requests, execution, review and reuse all happen in one shared issue pool: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raise a request] --> B[AI refines it
adds acceptance criteria] B --> C[Assign
yourself · a colleague · an agent] C --> D[Agent runs it
with a team plugin] D --> E[AI review
assignee confirms] E --> F[Requester signs off] F --> G[Save as a plugin] G -.reused by the team.-> D ``` | Role | Where they join | | --- | --- | | **Solo developer** | Puts requests in the pool, lets agents work through them, and only signs off | | **Specialist** | Gets a task right with AI, saves the method as a plugin, and publishes it to the team | | **Manager** | Drops in a request; AI fills in the criteria and routes it to a person or an agent; signs off at the end | | **New team member** | Uses the plugins the organization has built up to do the work to team standards, and improves them when they find a gap | Who asked, who did the work, which plugin ran and who approved it is always on record. ## Multi-harness · Multi-agent A harness is the agent runtime that does the work. It is not the model. SoduWork connects every harness through one adapter interface, so issues, plugins and review don't depend on any single harness. Switch harnesses mid-conversation and keep the history and the working folder. Programs that support the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) can be added with a catalog declaration.
Supported harnesses (7) | Harness | Models | How it connects | | --- | --- | --- | | Pi | Your SoduWork models | Built in | | OpenCode | Your SoduWork models | Native adapter, installed on demand | | DeepSeek Harness | Your SoduWork models, or your own DeepSeek key | ACP, installed on demand | | Qwen Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Kimi Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex Harness | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex | Its own OpenAI account | Native adapter, installed on demand |
Agents work together at several levels: | Level | Who decides | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | Harness | The harness itself | OpenCode or Qwen Code starts its own subagents to explore the code or split

repository.description: 🎮 Open-source, cross-platform 2D/3D/multiplayer game engine designed for everyone.

details.readme:
![GDevelop logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ian/GDevelop/master/newIDE/GDevelop%20banner.png "GDevelop logo")

GDevelop is a **full-featured, no-code, open-source** game development software. You can build **2D, 3D and multiplayer games** for mobile (iOS, Android), desktop and the web. GDevelop is designed to be fast and incredibly intuitive: make games using an easy-to-understand yet powerful event-based system and modular behaviors. Create with AI that assists or builds alongside you.

![The GDevelop editor when editing a game level](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ian/GDevelop/master/newIDE/GDevelop%20screenshot.png "The GDevelop editor when editing a 3D game level")

![The GDevelop editor when editing a game level](./newIDE/GDevelop%202D%20screenshot.png "The GDevelop editor when editing a 2D game level")

## Getting started

| ❔ I want to...                                   | 🚀 What to do                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 🎮 Use GDevelop to make games                     | Go to [GDevelop homepage](https://gdevelop.io) to download the app!                                                                                               |
| ⚙️ Create/improve an extension                    | Read about [creating an extension](https://wiki.gdevelop.io/gdevelop5/extensions/create), with no-code or code.                                                   |
| 🧑‍💻 Contribute to the editor or game engine        | Follow this [README](newIDE/README.md).                                                                                                                           |
| 👾 Create or sell a game template                 | Submit a [free example or a paid template on the Asset Store](https://wiki.gdevelop.io/gdevelop5/community/guide-for-submitting-an-example/).                     |
| 🎨 Share or sell an asset pack                    | Submit a [free or paid asset pack on the Asset Store](https://wiki.gdevelop.io/gdevelop5/community/sell-asset-pack-store).                                        |
| 🌐 Help translate GDevelop                        | Go on the [GDevelop project on Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/gdevelop) or translate [in-app tutorials](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-tutorials). |
| 👥 Get online game services or commercial support | See offers for [professionals, teams or individual creators](https://gdevelop.io/pricing).                                                                        |

> Are you interested in contributing to GDevelop for the first time? Take a look at the list of **[good first issues](https://github.com/4ian/GDevelop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22%F0%9F%91%8Cgood+first+issue%22)**, **[good first contributions](https://github.com/4ian/GDevelop/discussions/categories/good-first-contribution)** or the **["🏐 not too hard" cards](https://trello.com/b/qf0lM7k8/gdevelop-roadmap?menu=filter&filter=label:Not%20too%20hard%20%E2%9A%BD%EF%B8%8F)** on the Roadmap.

## Games made with GDevelop

- Find GDevelop games on [gd.games](https://gd.games), the gaming platform for games powered by GDevelop.
- See the [showcase of games](https://gdevelop.io/games) created with GDevelop and published on Steam, iOS (App Store), Android (Google Play), Itch.io, Newgrounds, CrazyGames, Poki...

[![Some games made with GDevelop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ian/GDevelop/master/newIDE/GDevelop%20games.png "Some games made with GDevelop")](https://gdevelop.io/games)

## Technical architecture

GDevelop is composed of an **editor**, a **game engine**, an **ecosystem** of extensions as well as **online services** and commercial support.

| Directory     | ℹ️ Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Core`        | Core classes, describing the structure of a game and tools to implement the IDE and work with GDevelop games.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `GDJS`        | The game engine, written in TypeScript, using PixiJS and Three.js for 2D and 3D rendering (WebGL), powering all GDevelop games.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `GDevelop.js` | Bindings of `Core`, `GDJS` and `Extensions` to JavaScript (with WebAssembly), used by the IDE.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `newIDE`      | The game editor, written in JavaScript with React, Electron, PixiJS and Three.js.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Extensions`  | Built-in extensions for the game engine, providing objects, behaviors and new features. For example, this includes the physics engines running in WebAssembly (Box2D or Jolt Physics for 3D). All the [official and experimental extensions are on this repository](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-extensions). [Community extensions are available here](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-community-list). |

To learn more about GDevelop Architecture, read the [architecture overview here](Core/GDevelop-Architecture-Overview.md).

Pre-generated documentation of the game engine is [available here](https://docs.gdevelop.io).

Status of the tests and builds: [![macOS and Linux build status](https://circleci.com/gh/4ian/GDevelop.svg?style=shield)](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/4ian/GDevelop) [![Fast tests status](https://gdevelop.semaphoreci.com/badges/GDevelop/branches/master.svg?style=shields)](https://gdevelop.semaphoreci.com/projects/GDevelop) [![Windows Build status](https://ci.appveyor.com/api/projects/status/84uhtdox47xp422x/branch/master?svg=true)](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/4ian/gdevelop/branch/master) [![https://good-labs.github.io/greater-good-affirmation/assets/images/badge.svg](https://good-labs.github.io/greater-good-affirmation/assets/images/badge.svg)](https://good-labs.github.io/greater-good-affirmation)

## Links

### Community

- [GDevelop forums](https://forum.gdevelop.io) and [Discord chat](https://discord.gg/gdevelop).
- [GDevelop homepage](https://gdevelop.io).
- [GDevelop wiki (documentation)](https://wiki.gdevelop.io/gdevelop5/start).
- Help translate GDevelop in your language: [GDevelop project on Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/gdevelop).
- Open-source [extensions (official or experimental)](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-extensions), [community extensions](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-community-list), [examples](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-examples), [tutorials](https://github.com/GDevelopApp/GDevelop-tutorials) are on GitHub.

details.readme:
The open-source studio for making games with AI.

English | 简体中文 | 日本語

Website · Docs · Community games · Changelog

Describe a game, and the agent designs it, makes the art, writes the code, plays it to check it works, and publishes it to a link anyone can open. Design docs, images, video, 3D, and audio live on one canvas next to the code, instead of across five different apps. > [!NOTE] > OhMyGame is in beta. Expect rough edges, and tell us what breaks. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS (Apple silicon) | [OhMyGame for Mac](https://ohmygame.ai/download/mac) | | Windows (x64) | [OhMyGame for Windows](https://ohmygame.ai/download/windows) | Older builds and release notes are on [Releases](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/releases). The Windows build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn on first install. Intel Mac and Linux are [on the roadmap](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues). OhMyGame ships without a model. On first launch, connect a provider or a coding agent you already use: [first run](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/first-run/). ## Features - **Let the agent build the game.** The agent drafts the design doc, writes the code, runs the game in a live preview, then plays it and tries a fix when something breaks. - **One canvas for every asset.** Generate images, video, 3D models, animation, voices, sound effects, and music with AI, and keep them organized on one canvas, ready to use in your game. - **Publish to a link.** Anyone can play it in the browser, and it shows up in the [Community](https://ohmygame.ai/community/). A multiplayer game's rooms, and its players' sign-in, saves, and leaderboards, come with it. - **Extend it with plugins.** A plugin can teach the agent new skills, give it new tools, and add panels and project types to the app. Preinstalled plugins cover Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender, Aseprite, Tiled, and platforms like WeChat and Douyin Mini Games. Or [make your own](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/plugins/make/). - **Bring your own agent.** Run OhMyGame on Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, or on any of 40+ model providers with your own keys. No per-run credits. It works the other way too: use the canvas, media generation, and playtesting from your agent over MCP. [Models](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/models/) · [External agents](docs/external-agents.md) ## What you can make Three games our team made with OhMyGame:
Interactive film Island builder Deckbuilding roguelike
**Web games** (Phaser, Three.js, React Three Fiber) are the best place to start. **Interactive stories** cover visual novels, interactive films, and story games. **General games** work with any engine or stack. Web games can be **multiplayer**, from board and card games to realtime arenas, played online with friends with no server of your own. See [Multiplayer](docs/multiplayer.md). [Play what others made](https://ohmygame.ai/community/). ## Documentation Guides for using OhMyGame are at **[ohmygame.ai/docs](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/)**: [install](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/install/), [first run](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/first-run/), [models](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/models/), and [plugins](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/plugins/). Technical references live in this repo under [`docs/`](docs/README.md), such as the [runtime](docs/runtime.md), [coding agents](docs/coding-agents.md), [custom models](docs/custom-models.md), and the [plugin contract](docs/plugins.md). ## Build from source Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.2+ and Node.js 22.19+. ```bash git clone https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame.git cd ohmygame bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run dev # web renderer + local daemon bun run dev:desktop # or the Electron app ``` Builds from source send no telemetry. For branches, checks, and optional cloud setup, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Privacy Your projects and API keys stay on your machine, and prompts go straight to the providers you choose. You only need an account to publish. Release builds send usage data and crash reports. Turn both off with **Send usage data and crash reports** in **Settings → About**. See [logs and diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md). ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Branch from `dev` and open PRs against `dev`; `main` holds releases. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), pick up a [`help wanted`](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/labels/help%20wanted) issue, and report security problems privately through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Community [Discord](https://discord.gg/TkrgvGQ2Zc) · [QQ group 460706923](https://qun.qq.com/universal-share/share?ac=1&authKey=65LzSf96ttluVSAPzPKJvrsoQ0NSQHPJnhgJImnnqIik9uK64ljVd%2FzkRWb8Xanz&busi_data=eyJncm91cENvZGUiOiI0NjA3MDY5MjMiLCJ0b2tlbiI6InNUNWR3U05OeVlMZEVCK0YxNUNKckplazliYklGRnV6ZUZGM1NlV29vYVdKNGkrR2g2c28zNG1kdDFFcHllczMiLCJ1aW4iOiIyNDUxMjQwODEifQ%3D%3D&data=CQ5T4W2Ac1NWWg56dH_HQwixT7faVMm5Xq5kZsLgx9TDBGxeqs3mwXNLVUpO83oOUobc1qXBosRKYmWnziWboA&svctype=4&tempid=h5_group_info) · [Issues](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues) ## Star History ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). The OhMyGame name and logo are not covered by the license.

details.readme:
Langfuse Cloud · Self-Host · Demo

Docs · Report Bug · Feature Request · Changelog · Roadmap


Langfuse is an **open source AI engineering platform** for **agent evals and observability**. It is one open platform for every AI call your company makes and every agent your teams build: track usage and costs, **trace and evaluate** agents, and use production data to ship better AI. Use Langfuse Cloud or **self-host in minutes**; Langfuse is **battle-tested** at scale. Watch a quick demo of the project here: > ### 🧑‍💻 We're hiring > > Interested in contributing to Langfuse full-time? Langfuse is growing fast (we doubled the team in the last 6 months). Since January 2026 we're part of ClickHouse. We hire remotely, with offices in Berlin, San Francisco, Amsterdam, and New York. > **[See open roles →](https://langfuse.com/careers?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=hiring&utm_content=langfuse)** ## ✨ Core Features - [AI Observability](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview): Instrument your app and start ingesting traces to Langfuse, thereby tracking LLM calls and other relevant logic in your app such as retrieval, embedding, or agent actions. Inspect and debug complex logs and user sessions. Built on OpenTelemetry. Try the interactive [demo](https://langfuse.com/docs/demo) to see this in action. - [Prompt Management](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/overview) helps you centrally manage, version control, and collaboratively iterate on your prompts. Thanks to strong caching on server and client side, you can iterate on prompts without adding latency to your application. The [LLM Playground](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/playground) lets you test prompts and model configurations; when you see a bad result in tracing, you can jump straight to the playground to iterate on it. - [Skill Management](https://langfuse.com/docs/skill-management/overview) (beta) brings versioning and labels to agent skills: a `SKILL.md` with task instructions plus optional supporting files. Promote or roll back versions without changing application code, and link skill versions to the traces they produced. - [Evaluations](https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/overview) are key to the AI agent development workflow, and Langfuse adapts to your needs. It supports LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback collection, manual labeling, and custom evaluation pipelines via APIs/SDKs. Use [Datasets and Experiments](https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets) to build test sets and benchmarks for pre-deployment testing and continuous improvement. - [AI Gateway](https://langfuse.com/docs/gateway/overview) (beta) gives your organization one endpoint for calls to your model providers. Keep provider credentials in one place, hand out per-user or service account gateway keys, approve models centrally, track AI spend per user, key, and model, and record every call as a Langfuse trace. - [Metrics and Dashboards](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/overview): Track latency, cost, and quality across any dimension with [custom dashboards](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards), the metrics API, and alerts. - [Comprehensive API](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/overview): Langfuse is frequently used to power bespoke AI engineering workflows while using the building blocks provided by Langfuse via the API. An OpenAPI spec, typed SDKs for Python and JS/TS, the [Langfuse CLI](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli), and the [Langfuse Agent Skill](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill) for coding agents are available. ## 📦 Deploy Langfuse ### Langfuse Cloud Managed deployment by the Langfuse team, generous free tier, no credit card required. **[Sign up for Langfuse Cloud →](https://langfuse.com/cloud)** ### Self-Host Langfuse Run Langfuse on your own infrastructure: - [Docker Compose](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/docker-compose): Run Langfuse on your own machine or a single virtual machine in 5 minutes. The guide also covers configuring Docker log rotation so container logs don't fill up the disk. ```bash # Get a copy of the latest Langfuse repository git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git cd langfuse # Run the langfuse docker compose docker compose up ``` - [Kubernetes (Helm)](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/kubernetes-helm): Run Langfuse on a Kubernetes cluster using Helm. This is the preferred production deployment. - Terraform Templates: [AWS](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/aws), [Azure](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/azure), [GCP](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/gcp) - Community-maintained: [Render](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/render), [Railway](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/railway) See [self-hosting documentation](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting) to learn more about architecture and configuration options. > [!TIP] > **Self-hosting Langfuse?** Subscribe to the [self-hosting update list](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting#subscribe) to get an email about important features and new releases for open source Langfuse — self-hosting updates only, no marketing. ## 🔌 Integrations Langfuse is built on [OpenTelemetry](https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry), so any OpenTelemetry-instrumented application, framework, or collector can send traces to Langfuse. ### Main Integrations | Integration | Supports | Description | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | [OpenTelemetry](https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry) | Any language | Send OTLP traces from your application or OpenTelemetry Collector to Langfuse's OpenTelemetry endpoint. | | [Langfuse AI Gateway](https://langfuse.com/docs/gateway/overview) (beta) | Any OpenAI or Anthropic client | Route model calls through one endpoint to trace every call, keep provider keys in one place, and track cost without SDK or code changes. | | [SDK](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview) | Python, JS/TS | Manual instrumentation using the SDKs for full flexibility. | | [OpenAI](https://langfuse.com/integrations/model-providers/openai-py) | Python, JS/TS | Automated instrumentation using drop-in replacement of OpenAI SDK. | | [LangChain & LangGraph](https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/langchain) | Python, JS/TS | Automated instrumentation by passing callback handler to LangChain or LangGraph application. | | [LlamaIndex](https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/llamaindex) | Python | Automated instrumentation via LlamaIndex callback system. | | [Haystack](https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/haystack) | Python | Automated instrumentati

🎮 An Open Source Unity-like Engine! 🎮

1. [About The Project](#-about-the-project-) 2. [Features](#-features-) 3. [Getting Started](#-getting-started-) * [Prerequisites](#prerequisites) * [Installation](#installation) 4. [Contributing](#-contributing-) 5. [Acknowledgments](#-acknowledgments-) * [Contributors](#contributors-) * [Dependencies](#dependencies-) 6. [License](#-license-) # 📝 About The Project 📝 Prowl is an open-source, **[MIT-licensed](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Prowl/blob/main/LICENSE)** game engine developed in **pure C# in latest .NET**. It aims to provide a seamless transition for developers familiar with _Unity_ by maintaining a similar API while also following KISS and staying as small and customizable as possible. Prowl is currently in **1.0 Preview 5**, which brings a new Vulkan renderer, animation, navigation, VR and a rewritten asset system. Projects from earlier 1.0 previews are backed up and migrated automatically when opened (However this migration isnt gauranteed during Preview Releases always backup!). Until the final 1.0 release, further breaking changes are expected. ### [

Join our Discord server! 🎉

](https://discord.gg/BqnJ9Rn4sn) [![ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/R7B4280JI3) | ![Screenshot](https://i.imgur.com/khCaEB5.png) | ![Screenshot](https://i.imgur.com/qNeMvC4.jpeg) | | :-: | :-: | | ![image](https://i.imgur.com/xooqeDx.png) | ![image](https://i.imgur.com/zbCJOwI.png) | | ![UntitledFLightModel](https://i.imgur.com/TkJOmw9.png) | ![Untitled](https://i.imgur.com/BXn31d0.png) | | ![UntitledFLightModel](https://i.imgur.com/rLGLo7h.png) | ![Untitled](https://i.imgur.com/jbKCif2.png) | # ✨ Features ✨ - **General:** - Cross-Platform! Windows, Linux & Mac, for both the Editor and exported builds with Andriod under development! - Unity-like Editor & Scripting API - C# Scripting with .NET 11, compiled in process with Roslyn - GameObject & Component Architecture - **Prowl.Runtime works fully standalone from the Editor** - reference it directly and ship a game with zero Editor dependency - Custom Immediate Mode UI ([Paper](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology)), Editor built on top of [Origami](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) - Vector Graphics & Text Rendering via [Quill](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) - `GameTask` async API (`MainThread`, `WorkerThread`, `NextFrame`, `Delay`, `WaitUntil`) with per session cancellation - Roslyn analyzers that catch common scripting mistakes (component constructors, blocking waits, `?.` on engine objects) - Serialization via [Prowl.Echo](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) - Tags & Layers System - Scenes with `Scene.Environment` (sky, ambient, fog), async load handles, additive sections and persistent objects - Prefabs - Apply, Revert, Break Instance & Override Tracking - Input Action System with Composites & Processors - `.inputactions` assets with a dedicated editor - Action phases (Disabled / Started / Performed / Cancelled) - Composite bindings (WASD to Float2, D-pad, etc.) for keyboard, mouse, gamepad & XR controllers - GameObject-Based UI, including World Space UI - `RectTransform`-driven layout, Buttons, Toggles, Sliders, Dropdowns, layout groups, drag & drop event handlers - Math via [Prowl.Vector](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) - SIMD backed vectors, Matrices (`Float4x4`), Quaternions, Transform2D - Shapes: AABB, Bounds, Frustum, Cone, Ray, Plane, LineSegment, Rect - Mesh editing operators & Quadric mesh simplification - Frame Stats profiler with custom scopes - **Editor:** - Scene View, Hierarchy, Inspector, Project Browser, Console, Game View, Frame Stats - Custom Component Editors, Property Editors, and Scene View Editors - Transform Gizmos (Move, Rotate, Scale), shift drag to duplicate - Undo/Redo System - Dockable & Resizable Panels with Layout Persistence and Panel Maximize - Drag & Drop (Assets, GameObjects, Components) - Multi-Select & Search/Filtering in Editor Panels - Asset Thumbnail Generation & 3D Previews - Animation Graph, Avatar, Animation Curve & Gradient Editors, plus a Ragdoll Generator - Volume Profile, Input Action, Sprite and Terrain Editors - Rebindable Shortcut/Hotkey System - 12 built in Themes with Customizable Color Palettes, sizing and wallpapers - Playtest directly in the Editor - Hot-Reloading Scripts - Localization - English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish & Chinese - Managed & Native Plugins with Assembly Definitions - **Prowl CLI** - drive a running editor from scripts or AI agents, projects ship with agent skills - **Graphics Rendering:** - Vulkan via [Prowl.Graphite](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) (MoltenVK on macOS) - GPU Driven Renderer: render graph, dedicated render thread, bindless textures, vertex pulling, multi draw indirect - Camera relative rendering - H-Forward Lighting and cached static shadows - Render Features API and pluggable Camera Pipelines for custom passes and designs - Prism, a fully managed GLSL to SPIR-V compiler, with async variant compiles, a SPIR-V cache and shaders precompiled into builds - Lit & Unlit Shaders, Surface Shaders, Material Variants, Shader Keywords/Variants - HDR & PBR (Physically Based Rendering) - Metallic Workflow - Albedo, Normal, Surface (AO / Roughness / Metallic), Emission, Parallax, Translucency & Anisotropy - Compute Shaders & Compute Buffers - Mesh Renderer & Skinned Mesh Renderer with GPU Blendshapes - Line Renderer - Sprites, with Sprite Sheet slicing (Grid, Isometric & Automatic alpha-based slicing) and a dedicated Sprite Editor - Render Textures, Texture3D & Cubemaps - Lights: Directional, Point, Spot and Area (Rect, Disk, Tube) - Sphere lights, sun disk, Light Cookies & IES Profiles - Shadow Atlas with static caching and screen size driven resolution - Cascaded Shadow Maps for Directional Lights (up to 4 cascades) - Point Light Shadows - Hard, Tent & Contact Hardening shadow filters - Decals (Albedo, Normal & Mask) - Reflection Probes (Baked & Realtime) with box projection and a Sky Probe - UV-Unwrapping via [Prowl.Unwrapper](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology), Progressive Lightmapper via [Prowl.Photonic](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) - Baked Light Probes - Skies: Procedural Atmosphere, Gradient, Cubemap, Panorama & Six Sided - Volumetric Clouds & Volumetric Fog - Camera Stacking, Camera Cuts & Debug View Modes - Tonemapping (ACES, AgX, Reinhard, RomBinDaHouse, Uncharted 2) - Anti Aliasing: FXAA, SMAA & TAA - Volume based Post Processing with global & local volumes - Auto Exposure, Bloom, GTAO, Screen Space Reflections, Motion Blur, Depth of Field, God Rays - Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Film Grain, Color Grading, Color Lookup (LUT), Sharpen, Edge Detection, Pixelation - Custom Post Effects - Transparency & Refraction - Terrain System - Quadtree LOD - Heightmap & Splatmap Painting - Grass, Details & Trees - Holes - Particle System - Shape, Emission, Sub Emitters, Texture Sheet Animation, Trails, Collision, Forces, Over Lifetime and by Speed modules - Local & World Simulation Spaces - **Animation:** - `Animator` with Animation Graphs via [Prowl.Motion](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology), about 90 nodes - State Machines, Blend Spaces, Layers & Masks, Inertial Blending - Humanoid Avatars with Retargeting between rigs - IK (Two Bone, Look At, Aim), Foot Grounding, Root Motion & Warping - Active Ragdolls with muscles & pinning - **Physics:** - Physics using [Jitter Physics 2](https://github.com/notgiven688/jitterphysics2) - Colliders: Box, Sphere, Capsule, Cylinder, Cone, Mesh (Convex or Concave), Terrain - Wheel Collider with friction curves, weight transfer, Anti Roll Bars & per surface grip - Joints & Constraints: Ball Socket, Hinge Joint, Hinge Angle, Fixed Angle, Cone Limit, Distance Limit, Twist Angle, Prismatic, Universal, Point On Line, Point On Plane, Angular Motor, Linear Motor, Drive - Character Controller with moving platforms, custom gravity, steps & slopes - Trigger Volumes & Collision Callbacks - Collision Layers & Filtering (LayerMask) - Raycasting & Shape Query API - **Navigation:** - NavMesh via [Prowl.Recast](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology) - NavMesh Surfaces, Agents, Obstacles (carving), Links & Modifiers - Area costs, Crowd Steering, background baking & partial rebuilds - **Audio:** - Audio via miniaudio - Spatial 3D Audio with Attenuation & Doppler - Audio Mixers & Groups - Effect chain (Delay, Distortion, Biquad Filter, Reverb, Phaser) + custom `IAudioEffect` - **VR:** - Desktop VR through OpenXR (SteamVR, Meta and other runtimes) - Stereo rendering with multiview - Controllers, Haptics, Hand Tracking & Eye Gaze - World Space UI Pointers - **Asset Pipeline:** - GUID-Based Asset References with Meta Files - One object per asset, refilled in place on reimport - Import Caching & File Watching for Auto-Reimport - Custom Importers via Attributes - Sub-Assets with Deterministic GUIDs - Forward & Reverse Dependency Tracking - Async Loading & Residency Management with a memory budget - Runtime Asset Mounting (folders, zips, HTTP) and Runtime Importers for mods & user content - Supported Formats: - Models: GLTF, GLB, OBJ, FBX (via [Prowl.Clay](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology)) - Textures: PNG, JPG, BMP, GIF, TGA, TIFF, WEBP, PSD, DDS, EXR, HDR and more (via [Prowl.Aperture](https://github.com/ProwlEngine/Anthology)) - Audio: WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC - Fonts: TTF, OTF - **Build System:** - Build to Standalone Application - Packed Asset Files (.prowlpak) - Only exports used assets - Used Shader Variants precompiled into the build - Per-platform build profiles - Native AOT Player Builds (experimental) - Supports Windows, Mac & Linux (Andriod under development) - **Samples:** - HelloProwl, Rendering, ManyLights, Physics, Controller, Vehicle, Particle, Scripting, VRBasics & VR Showcases under `Samples/Runtime`
